held.title: An unset belief_time may stop the lookup from finding existing annotations, so repeat posts create duplicates.
held.body: The lookup now filters on `Annotation.belief_time == annotation.belief_time`. A caller may build an Annotation without a belief_time and leave it to a column default or server default applied at insert. Before flush, that object's `belief_time` is `None`, so the filter becomes `belief_time IS NULL`. It then never matches the stored row, which has a real timestamp. Each repeat of the same annotation would insert a new row with a new belief_time, where the old content/start/end lookup reused the existing row. I could not see the `Annotation` model or its callers, so I can't confirm whether `belief_time` gets a default. If it does, fill in the default before the lookup (for example in the constructor), or keep a fallback match for callers that give no belief time.

held.title: `scalar_one_or_none()` can raise MultipleResultsFound on existing rows that match the new, wider key.
held.body: Before this change, end was part of the lookup and belief_time was not, so the database may already hold rows that differ only in `end`. That can happen when belief_time is NULL, because PostgreSQL treats NULLs in a unique constraint as distinct, so the constraint does not block such rows. The new filter drops `end`, so a post for such an annotation matches several rows. `scalar_one_or_none()` then raises `MultipleResultsFound` and the request fails with HTTP 500. Whether such rows exist depends on the column's nullability and on existing data, which I could not see. Either handle more than one match (for example, order by id and take the first) or deduplicate those rows in a migration.
